ideas.title: [Rank 4] Is the LM's edge out of range? Titan+T2 vs matched-label no-LLM learners (S-roll MLP and a from-scratch digit-token transformer) on the OOD and long-horizon strata
ideas.evidence_basis:
- **Ledger k=4 regret:** S-roll FULL with the DEV-regret head reached 0.051 (4,245 transitions, pilot), vs T2 ON 0.056 on confirm2 and 0.038 on pilot with 384 + 1,501 oracle rows.
- S-roll catches Titan by about 512 transitions (R10, replicated in R11).
- The S-roll caveats name the gap: "one learner family, no copy mechanism, no digit inputs".
- PREREG-2's registered limit: "No comparison with non-LM learners at the same label budget".
- REPORT §6: the LM's edge is copying and data efficiency, measured in distribution only.
ideas.design:
- **Compute:** CPU only, 6 threads, below-normal priority, respecting the >= 12 GB RAM floor for CPU lanes (D-39).
- **Training data:** exactly the ledger rows Titan+T2 saw (Titan's 128 ledger rows + T2's 501 ledger rows), plus FULL as a reference.
- **Learners:**
  - S-roll MLP with the frozen s_roll.py configs, both selection rules;
  - a 2-4-layer, 5-20M-parameter character/digit-token seq2seq transformer trained from scratch on the same JSON in/out. It can copy, and its grid and checkpoint are selected on pilot DEV only.
- **Evaluation:**
  - on the Rank-1 strata each learner can represent (magnitudes and operands for both; key renaming and extra accounts for the transformer only);
  - on the Rank-2 k = 8/16 clamped and natural chains.
- **Titan numbers:** reused from Ranks 1 and 2 (no extra GPU). Learners are trained and frozen before Titan's OOD outputs are read.
- **Primary contrast:** Titan+T2 minus the best no-LLM learner on k = 4/8/16 regret and one-step exact, per OOD stratum.
ideas.improves:
- This tests generalisation directly, and it decides where LM-based world models are worth their cost. It is the most strategy-relevant comparison the programme has not run.
- An LM edge out of range justifies continued LM-simulator work.
- No edge redirects the programme toward "LM for parsing and textual rules + learned or symbolic simulator".
ideas.risks:
- The from-scratch transformer's tuning burden invites fairness disputes. Register the grid and DEV-only selection.
- Comparisons on strata the MLP cannot represent are asymmetric. Report these as "not representable" rather than as wins.
- CPU contention with the peer's CPU lanes is possible.
- Titan's training rows come from a different (Forge v2) distribution, a known S-roll caveat.
ideas.test_plan:
- **Pre-registered:** learner families, grids, seeds (5 per learner), DEV-only selection and the contrast.

ideas.title: [Rank 5] A re-mintable, correctness-based retention suite, and calibrating KL drift against actual capability loss
ideas.hypothesis:
First-token KL and greedy agreement measure how far behaviour moves, not what is lost.
- The T2 adapter's drift concentrates on numeric reasoning, where correctness can be graded.
- Predictions: correctness losses for T2 ON concentrate in arithmetic-chain, unit-conversion, counting and time categories, and in literal-UNKNOWN abstention for every Titan arm.
- Per-prompt KL predicts per-item correctness flips poorly (AUROC < 0.65), so the KL gates C5 (L1) and the PREREG-2 guard are miscalibrated as forgetting gates.
ideas.evidence_basis:
- **T2_RESULTS F (adapter OFF vs ON):** the largest KL classes are arithmetic_chain 0.279, unit_conversion 0.245, counting_sets 0.173 and time_duration 0.150 nats. arithmetic_chain greedy agreement is 0.00 (4/4 replies changed).
- **PREREG-2 guard:** PASS at 0.50x, but cumulative KL(Supa‖ON) is 1.94x and Supa/ON 64-token agreement is 0.37.
- **Titan-Sparse's abstention damage** (RCI-001: 25/128 vs 40/128, p 6.1e-5) went unflagged by drift metrics.
- **The adapter wrecks an in-domain skill:** prerequisite applicable state-changing steps fall from 0.59 to 0.35 (D3), with no off-task signal.
- **L1 states there is no unspent confirmation capacity for retention claims** (gap G9), and there is no read budget for selection banks (gap G1).
ideas.improves:
- Retention of existing abilities, measured as correctness rather than drift.
- It recalibrates every gate the programme uses (L1 C5, PREREG-2's guard), and provides the missing retention evidence for packaging both the T2 adapter and the BWM adapters.
ideas.risks:
- Templated tasks are narrow and do not cover conversational quality.
- The 0.6B base may be weak in some categories, so select on Supa only to avoid floors.
- Grading without an LLM judge limits the category set.
- Generator banks must be registered so they never enter training data.
- L8-15 needs its built arm file (it exists under runs/l1_screen/arm-l8_15).
ideas.test_plan:
- **Freeze first:** generator code, category list, margins (for example net loss <= 5 of 75 per category vs the parent) and the analysis.
- **Mint after the freeze:** a fresh confirmation seed.
- **Primary:** per-arm, per-category net loss vs Supa and vs the parent, exact McNemar, Holm over categories.
- **Secondary:** KL-loss AUROC with a bootstrap CI.
- **Records:** registry entries (SELECTION / CONFIRMATION, read budget) are written at first use, closing the G1 pattern. Operator approval is needed before any use in a promotion decision.
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- BWM's local devfreeze package (D-49) puts unmerged LoRAs (delta BW_F, BW_Pa_v2) on the same Titan-Sparse core and has no retention evidence at all.
- The same suite and the router false-positive test serve both packages. One extra arm costs about 0.2 GPU-h each, and the generator code can be shared.

ideas.title: [Rank 6, speculative] Does one-step rule training compose latently? Single-shot k-step answers and teacher-forced likelihood ranking under the T2 adapter
ideas.hypothesis:
Speculative. The T2 adapter was trained only on one-step rows.
- If it also lifts single-shot (e2e) multi-step answers above the independent-composition null (the product of per-step accuracies), the rule has become internally composable, a latent world model. That would reopen the latent-consequence line PREREG-1 closed (latent heads 0.75-0.97 regret).
- If the density ranks the true k-step consequence above heuristic foils even where generation fails, composition is present but not decodable by greedy generation.
- Default expectation from RCWM-T1 is negative: ON e2e exact at k=4 <= 0.15 while chained is 0.70.
ideas.evidence_basis:
- R6: e2e collapses faster than independent composition (L at k=2: 0.072 vs 0.39^2 ≈ 0.15).
- PREREG-1 C4: chaining beats single-shot by 0.33-0.47 regret at k=4.
- The likelihood-ranking instrument (D-09, run_lik.py) never finished: lik_log.txt shows the Titan-Sparse run completed and the Supa run left waiting for the lease, with no analysis file in runs/bank_pilot/analysis.
- L chain_m1 transfer (multi-event frame, one event at a time) was strong (+0.744 at k=4), so the multi-step frame itself is not the barrier.
- The serial-computation limits cited in RELATED_WORK predict a negative result.
ideas.design:
- **Parents:** the Rank-2 bank's 120 ledger parents x 8 plans, using prefixes at k = 2, 4 and 8.
- **(i) e2e single-shot:** in the multi-step frame (SYSTEM_MULTI), adapter ON vs OFF; about 5,760 generations, about 0.5 h.
- **(ii) Teacher-forced likelihood ranking** of the gold k-step state against equal-token-length foils:
  - copy s0, ignore-status, last-event-only;
  - the model's own chained prediction;
  - gold with one account perturbed by +-amount.
  - Metrics: rank-1 rate and mean log-prob margin, ON vs OFF, at k = 1, 2, 4, 8.
- **Null:** the product of per-step accuracies from Rank 2.
- **Self-consistency:** whether the density prefers the model's own chained prediction over gold when the two differ.
ideas.improves:
This is a compositional generalisation test: composing a learned rule without being trained to.
- A positive result would change direction toward cheaper latent planning (no serial calls).
- A negative result settles the explicit-rollout stance for both programmes and retires the remaining latent-head work.
ideas.risks:
- The multi-step frame is untrained for T2, so frame effects confound e2e. The chain_m1 transfer suggests this is manageable.
- Likelihood is sensitive to token length and number formatting, so foils must match length and the margins be normalised.
- A negative result is likely, so the expected information is lower.
ideas.test_plan:
- **Registered directional predictions:**
  - ON e2e exact at k=4 <= product-law null + 0.05;
  - ON likelihood rank-1 at k=4 >= OFF + 0.10.
- **Statistics:** parent-paired bootstrap, Holm over the two.
- **Bank:** shared with Rank 2. The likelihood instrument is the existing D-09 code, re-hashed and frozen.
- **Label:** exploratory unless both predictions are registered before any output.
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- This is the planning-side twin of BWM's T-effect question: do proposers benefit from explicit state supervision (the A10/A11 arms)?
- If latent composition appears under rule-coverage training, BWM should test whether BW_F training improves Pa_v2's direct (no-F) plans on val_large (currently 0.117).
- If not, both programmes standardise on explicit rollout plus search, and stop budgeting for latent variants.

ideas.title: FlagWorld bridge: give the prerequisite simulator BWM's explicit-legality bit/delta interface instead of Titan's integer mask
ideas.evidence_basis:
- R10/R11: Titan is right on 383/415 applicable steps where state+add equals the bitwise result, and on 2/333 where it does not.
- PREREG-2 (runs/bank_confirm2/analysis/PREREG_2_RESULTS.md): P false copy +0.558; applicable state-changing steps 0.587 -> 0.353; unchanged 0.027 -> 0.767; inapplicable 0.032 -> 0.879; k=4 exact 0.205 vs copy floor 0.117.
- My read-only check of runs/t2/t2_s0/gen_pilot.jsonl (4,819 oracle-anchored one-step rows, OFF vs ON):
  - P applicable-changing with integer-add wrong (n=86): OFF 0.06, ON 0.00, either 0.06;
  - applicable-no-change (n=194): OFF 0.02 (67% exactly state+add), ON 0.78;
  - inapplicable (n=347): ON 0.90.
  - The best possible per-step ON/OFF router reaches only 0.77 vs ON 0.70, so BWM-style deferral cannot repair P; the representation has to change.
- BWM F-05/F-07: with about 50% illegal rows, Blocksworld legality is 0.997 in distribution. The delta format removed long-state copy errors (15 blocks 0.967 -> 1.000).
- bwm/code/bwmn/flags.py, flags_planner.py and scripts/flags_run.py already implement exactly this family (Forge v2 prerequisite_plan) with bitstring states, {legal,state,terminated} targets, BFS and a proposer pipeline. None of it has ever been run.
- My structural audit: 3,555 of 4,800 (74%) bank_confirm2 P chain steps are identical, up to bit permutation, to a T2 training row. A bitstring arm therefore needs a dedupe that is invariant to bit permutation.
ideas.improves: Rule learning (preconditions and delete semantics), multi-step consequence accuracy on the weakest family, size generalisation out of range, and planning in a STRIPS-style domain shared by both programmes.
ideas.risks:
- Gains could come from the new interface, or from 'just a LoRA', rather than from rule learning. A-int controls for the data; add a Supa-base arm later to test whether Titan's delta matters.
- C-delta applies the change by parser. This is deterministic and legitimate, but it must be disclosed.
- Bitstrings may invite per-position copy shortcuts; false copy is measured to catch this.
- Bit-permutation structural overlap could inflate the bits arms. Mitigate by structural dedupe and by size-OOD as the cleanest test.
- Longer outputs (about 20 vs 3 tokens) raise the decode cost.
- One seed until replicated.
ideas.test_plan:
1. Exploratory pilot on a DEV-only bank.
2. If the best format beats A-int by >= +0.25 on k=4 exact, train 2 more seeds (the T2 precedent).
3. PREREG with these primaries, Holm m=2, one-sided 95% bounds:
   - (best format - A-int) on P chain_m1 k=4 exact >= +0.25;
   - on the int-add-wrong one-step stratum >= +0.50.
   Size-OOD and FlagWorld planning are secondary (BH q=0.10). Directional predictions D: A-int lowers false copy vs T2 but leaves int-add-wrong < 0.20.
4. Bank: fresh and sealed, built with no model call, excluded by payload + operative key + bit-permutation signature against all RCWM banks, T2 files, SELECT-VIEWS-001 and the L1 A-OOD bank (ac665c11). HSKILL_CONFIRM_V2 is skipped by name.
5. Parity gate: OFF reproduces Titan-Sparse's stored P chains byte for byte.
6. Run under the lease and thermal rules.
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- BWM's dormant FlagWorld code is RCWM's prerequisite family under BWM's contracts, so it becomes a shared domain. RCWM brings sealed banks and the per-operation failure map; BWM brings the explicit-legality/delta format and the beam/BFS planner.
- The result decides whether both programmes' world models should standardise on explicit-legality delta outputs. BWM already found that format fixes long-state copy errors in Blocksworld.

ideas.title: Search under the learned simulator: does PREREG-2's near-oracle ledger model survive BWM-style planning, and can BWM's confidence signal curb exploitation?
ideas.hypothesis:
Ranking 8 fixed plans understates simulator error. When a planner searches a larger plan space, the selected plan's predicted utility overestimates its true utility more and more (winner's curse / model exploitation):
- For imperfect simulators (Titan-Sparse OFF on ledger; register, where mix is about 0.01 in both arms) the absolute loss grows with search breadth.
- T2-ON ledger stays near-oracle: normalised regret <= 0.10 with 81 candidates.
- Pessimistic selection using BWM-style confidence (per-step answer-token log-prob margin), U_pred - lambda*sum(step uncertainty), cuts the exploitation gap of the imperfect simulators by >= 30% without hurting ON.
- Search exposes systematic blind spots (S-roll's scale 0.09) that 8-plan ranking hides.
ideas.evidence_basis:
- My read-only analysis of the stored bank_confirm2 chains (rcwmt.decide.regret_table, random candidate subsets): K=8 reproduces PREREG-2 exactly (L OFF 0.544, ON 0.056; R OFF 0.348, ON 0.329).
- Exploitation gap (predicted minus true utility of the chosen plan) at K = 2 / 4 / 8:
  - ledger OFF +0.130 / +0.248 / +0.356 (absolute loss 0.134 -> 0.371, nearly 3x);
  - ledger ON +0.012 / +0.022 / +0.031;
  - register OFF +0.075 -> +0.187 and ON +0.076 -> +0.181 (mix unfixed).
  - Normalised regret stays flat (0.526 -> 0.544) because the oracle's gain also grows. The metric hides the exploitation.
- PREREG-1: decision quality comes from partially correct states (k=4 exact 0.024 L / 0.092 R).
- S-roll FULL with DEV-regret selection reaches 0.051 on pilot L, tying T2-ON, despite a scale blind spot (0.09) (R10).
- BWM P-06: every F-verified Blocksworld plan was valid (precision 1.00). F-02: the legality-token margin flags F errors at AUROC 0.923. F-04: confidence-based deferral helps; random deferral at the same rate hurts (0.847 < 0.886). P-05: success-vs-compute frontier accounting.
ideas.improves: Planning quality with a learned world model, the robustness of decisions to model error under search, and calibrated use of the simulator. This is the step from 'rank given plans' to 'find plans'.
ideas.risks:
- Normalised regret is not comparable across K, so absolute loss is pre-registered as primary.
- Tree-structured candidates correlate errors (realistic for search, but it reduces the effective n).
- Greedy token log-prob may be a weak uncertainty signal for multi-digit numbers. BWM's 0.923 AUROC was for a boolean token, so report AUROC per operation.
- Logging log-probs changes the generation code. A parity gate must show identical greedy texts.
- Beam search with a linear goal readout may need a per-goal search. Restrict beam search to 16 DEV-selected goals if the cost explodes.
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- This literally puts RCWM's confirmed simulator inside BWM's planning machinery: tree caching, beam-in-imagination, F-call accounting and confidence signals.
- It also gives BWM a quantitative exploitation instrument it lacks. Blocksworld's 1.00 verification precision comes from a near-exact F; this test measures what happens to planning value as F degrades.
- That informs BWM's choice of beam width versus F quality.

ideas.title: Core-transfer test: is Titan-Sparse (or L8-15) a better substrate than Supa for learning new world models?
ideas.hypothesis:
Titan's 384-row delta installs a reusable state-update/copy prior in blocks 8-15. It should make new world-model adapters more data-efficient.
- At small budgets (<= 750 rows), a Blocksworld forward LoRA on Titan-Sparse should beat the same LoRA on Supa 1.7 by >= 0.05 exact at 10-15 blocks, the copy-heavy regime. The gap should close by about 3,000 rows.
- L8-15 should be non-inferior to Titan-Sparse (margin -0.03). The shared core could then move to the less-drifting L8-15 without retraining cost to BWM.
- Secondary: the T2 rule-coverage recipe on Supa should reach lower ledger k=4 exact than on Titan (0.698).
ideas.evidence_basis:
- R10: Titan's edge over a generic learner is exact copying (register swap 1.00 vs 0.00) and small-budget data efficiency (ledger -0.185 [-0.317, -0.051] at 128 rows; gone by 512).
- R12/R14: the skill lives in blocks 8-15; L8-15 keeps it with drift 0.68x [0.62, 0.74].
- PREREG-2 limit: 'Titan-Sparse only', so whether the base matters is untested.
- BWM F-05: BW_F errors at 12-15 blocks (0.967) are copy errors in long fact lists.
- D-28: the Titan-Sparse core stays byte for byte because the peer's adapters depend on it, but that dependence has never been measured.
- BWM F-02: with the adapter off, Titan answers |2x|<=L correctly on 94/96 flips. Whether that is Titan's or Supa's competence is unknown, yet it underpins the F-03 repair.
- Throughput: BW_Fdelta trained at about 9.9 s/step (600 steps in 5,944 s); T2 took 190 steps in 1,865 s.
ideas.improves: Data efficiency of acquiring new world models, size generalisation, and the choice of shared core for both programmes, including whether retention-friendlier L8-15 can serve as the world-model base.
ideas.risks:
- Supa's answer-format prior (it wraps as {before,after}) may cost early steps. Parse failures are scored separately, and a 50-step format check is included.
- One seed. Run a second seed only if a gap >= 0.05 appears.
- L8-15 must not read L1's reserved instruments (A-OOD bank, 456 fresh drift prompts), and this run must not interfere with the frozen L1 screen or BWM's frozen B2 shards. It uses new keys only and leaves frozen adapters untouched.
- Learning-rate sensitivity across bases is possible. Keep the recipe fixed and disclose that.
ideas.test_plan:
1. Preregister:
   - primary: Titan - Supa exact at 12-15 blocks at 750 rows (paired by key; McNemar + key-cluster bootstrap);
   - L8-15 - Titan non-inferiority at margin -0.03;
   - secondary: the curve shape and the T2-on-Supa contrast.
2. Fresh keys from an unused generator seed with BWM's renaming-signature exclusion against PlanBench-600, hard-110 and all training rows.
3. 2 seeds before any claim.
4. Report both the adapter-on drift and the base's own drift vs Supa on a NEW fresh off-task prompt draw (not R14's 248 or L1's 456).
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- This directly tests the premise of a 'Titan world-model core'. If Titan's delta speeds up BWM's adapters, RCWM's 384-row skill becomes infrastructure for BWM.
- If it does not, BWM can train on Supa or L8-15 freely, and D-28's byte-freeze constraint can be relaxed.
- It also establishes whether BWM's frozen-base verifier competence (F-02) comes from Titan's delta or from Supa.

ideas.title: One shared world-model adapter across domains, localised to blocks 8-15 (unified-core test; partly speculative)
ideas.hypothesis:
(a) A single joint LoRA trained on the union of RCWM T2 rows (1,501), BWM Blocksworld delta-F rows (3,000 subsample) and RW2 forward rows (1,455) matches each per-domain adapter within 0.03 on that domain's primary metric. In other words, world-model skills share capacity without interference.
(b) Restricting it to blocks 8-15, where R12 localised the transition computation, keeps >= 95% of each skill and cuts cumulative off-task drift from 1.94x to <= 1.3x KL(Supa||Sparse).
(c) SPECULATIVE: BWM rows with an explicit `legal` flag and about 50% illegal transfer a domain-general 'check preconditions, else unchanged' behaviour that lowers RCWM P false copy (T2-ON 0.624) and raises R conditional boundary accuracy (0.33-0.55).
ideas.evidence_basis:
- PREREG-2 forgetting guard: first-token KL(OFF||ON) is 0.50x Titan's own drift, but cumulative KL(Supa||ON) is 1.94x [1.77, 2.18], and 64-token agreement Supa/ON is 0.37 vs Supa/Sparse 0.50.
- R12: delta in blocks 8-15 gives FR 0.85/1.00/0.97; blocks 16-27 are LO.
- R14: localisation keeps regret (L +0.017 [-0.127, 0.158]) at KL ratio 0.68.
- T2 is already a 3-family adapter that fixed L but not P or R.
- BWM adapters (F_titan_main 1,455 RW2 rows; BW_Fdelta_s0 12k rows; Pa_v2) use the same vendored trainer (bwmn/lm.py attach_lora: r16 on q,k,v,o,gate,up,down) on the same frozen Titan-Sparse, so the data pool directly. peft's layers_to_transform makes block localisation a one-line change.
- BWM F-05/F-07: legality 0.997 in distribution with explicit legal targets.
ideas.improves: Retention of existing abilities while adding world models, capacity sharing across domains, and possibly cross-domain transfer of legality rules. This is the step toward a single deployable world-model core.
ideas.risks:
- Joint training may need more steps or reweighting. Blocksworld rows dominate tokens, so cap per-domain token shares.
- Blocks 8-15 may suffice for Titan's tiny skill but not for Blocksworld's long outputs; the per-domain breakdown shows this.
- (c) is speculative: the formats differ, and transfer may be nil.
- If adapters are only ever switched on explicitly by the planner, drift matters less. The retention claim is relevant to an always-on or merged core, and should be stated that way.
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- This is the concrete 'unified small-model world-model core': one frozen base plus one localised world-model adapter serving RCWM simulators, BWM's RW2 and Blocksworld F, and the planner.
- RCWM contributes the mechanism (where to put the parameters) and the drift instrument, which BWM has never applied to its adapters. BWM contributes the largest and most legality-rich training set and the size-generalisation grading.

ideas.title: Micro-step rollout for composite operations: chain BWM-proven primitive ops inside one register event (speculative)
ideas.hypothesis:
Register mix (r += 2*other + v mod 97) and modular wrap fail because they compose three operations and a modulo in a single answer.
- If the simulator writes intermediate primitive results (2*other, +v, +r, mod 97) as a short scratchpad or micro-event chain, it should learn mix from the same budget. These primitives are of the kind BWM's RW2 world model extrapolates at 99.5%.
- Targets: mix one-step >= 0.60 (now 0.01-0.03 for both arms); wrap >= 0.60 (0.22-0.32 with T2); R chain k=4 regret drop >= 0.10 (T2 gave -0.019).
- This applies RCWM's own finding that external chaining beats single-shot (2.8-17x), at a finer grain.
ideas.evidence_basis:
- PREREG-2 step accuracy: mix/nowrap 0.022 -> 0.022, mix/wrap 0.013 -> 0.009, add/wrap 0.000 -> 0.318; R k=4 regret ON-OFF -0.019, D4 holds.
- My T2_s0 pilot-row check: the mix 'either arm correct' bound is 0.02-0.03, so no routing can help.
- R11: upward wraps output the unreduced sum r+v (9/9), so the model adds but omits the mod.
- R6: chaining beats e2e 2.8-17x on L and R.
- BWM F-01: F_LM arithmetic 0.995 on unseen numbers (add1/sub1/double/halve) but 0.907 on three-digit outputs. BWM D-27 planned an A3 scratchpad arm.
ideas.design:
Two LoRAs on Titan-Sparse, using the same 600 fresh R rows (mix 300 including single and double wraps, add-wrap 150, conditional boundary 150):
- (a) direct state target;
- (b) scratchpad target {t:2*other, u:t+value, raw:register+u, mod:raw mod 97, after:{...}}, with only `after` parsed.

Optional arm (c): micro-event chain. The harness feeds the model's own intermediate value back as the next micro-step, exactly like chain_one.

Eval on a fresh R bank:
- one-step strata (mix nowrap/wrap1/wrap2, add-wrap, boundary, swap/add retention);
- chain_one k=4 exact and regret.
ideas.improves: Composite arithmetic and rule learning in the register family, the only family neither the T2 adapter nor the routing bound helps. This makes the shared simulator compositional.
ideas.risks:
- Speculative.
- The scratchpad lengthens decoding (about 3x tokens per step), which raises the cost of every downstream planner call.
- Errors in intermediates compound inside the step.
- Mod-97 on three-digit raw sums is exactly BWM's weaker stratum (0.907).
- It may still fail at about 300 mix rows.
ideas.test_plan:
1. Exploratory pilot with 1 seed. If (b) or (c) beats (a) by >= +0.4 on mix, run 2 more seeds, then a PREREG on a fresh sealed R bank (no model call; payload, operative and renaming exclusion).
2. Primaries: mix one-step exact and R k=4 regret, Holm m=2.
3. Retention check: swap and add/nowrap must not drop by more than 0.03.
ideas.bwm_synergy:
- The improved register simulator plugs straight into the shared planner of idea 2.
- It tests BWM's open A3 question (scratchpad vs direct targets) on a harder composite rule, with RCWM's sealed-bank evaluation.
- The synergy is weaker than in ideas 1-5; it is included because register is the one family where neither programme's current tools help.

scores.title: 1. Put the intermediate in the answer: trace-in-JSON targets for rules that need a computed value (register conditional, mix/mod-97, prerequisite applicability)
scores.rationale: This targets the actual remaining failures: R mix is about 0.05 even with no wrap, the conditional is at chance (0.55, boundary pairs 0.00), and P bitwise cells sit at 0.00. The filler arm cleanly separates supervision from extra compute, but re-rendering T2's exact events keeps the 66% copy-target P mix and only 175 mix rows, and the arm costs the most GPU time of the trace arms (5 h).

scores.title: 2. Shortcut-neutralised, minimal-pair prerequisite data to break the copy shortcut
scores.rationale: Making the P heuristics uninformative is good anti-shortcut practice, but Titan's P rule is integer addition (2/333 correct where state+add differs from the bitwise answer), and bare decimal answers need bitwise operations in a single pass. The most likely outcome is chance or a new shortcut, and the FlagWorld A-int arm and the scratchpad ideas test this more efficiently.

scores.title: 3. Separate rule learning from frame adaptation and targeting: self-distillation, natural-marginal (untargeted) and void-dose controls for PREREG-2's gain
scores.rationale: This closes a registered PREREG-2 limit, and the dose curve helps plan future data budgets, but it attributes a ledger gain that is already near-oracle rather than adding any capability, at 4 GPU h.

scores.title: 4. Rule or token? Lexical and rule-text counterfactual probes for 'status is not posted', then counterfactual-augmented training
scores.rationale: Training saw only 'posted' and 'void', so whether T2 learned the stated rule or a void-token trigger is the key test of real rule learning. Part (a) is cheap (about 0.6 GPU h), and part (b) trains for held-out words and inverted rule text, which is the kind of generalisation the goal asks for.

scores.title: 5. Matched-budget data-efficiency curves: Titan LoRA vs the S-roll MLP vs a copy-capable symbolic learner
scores.rationale: Locating where the LM's data-efficiency edge ends is strategically useful, but it is comparative positioning on in-distribution ledger data, where S-roll already catches up by about 512 rows, and it makes no model smarter.

scores.title: 6. Rehearsal data inside the rule-coverage LoRA to stop cumulative drift (speculative on magnitude)
scores.rationale: Rehearsal is a standard and plausible way to cut the 1.94x cumulative drift, but D-28(b) already keeps T2 unmerged and ledger-scoped, so always-on drift matters less. The rehearsal pool is also hard to build under the instrument exclusions.

scores.title: Disagreement-certified verification to stretch ledger rollouts to 8-16 steps (T2 adapter, no new training)
scores.rationale: Seed voting may lift long-horizon ledger exact accuracy, but it is a 3x inference-compute gain on a family that is already near-oracle, not a durable capability, and 5 GPU h is expensive. Seeds trained on the same rows will share their shortcuts out of range, as BWM F-06 warns.

scores.title: Zero-training register fix: mod-97 output tool, a comparison sub-query, and model-written expressions run by a calculator
scores.rationale: This is cheap, and the held-out-op and modulus-89 strata are good rule-reading guards, but most of the gain would come from the tool rather than the model. A 0.6B model writing correct mix expressions zero-shot is unlikely, so it adds little durable model intelligence.

scores.title: Binary scratchpad inside each step for the prerequisite family, against a direct-answer LoRA trained on the same rows
scores.rationale: It turns P's bitwise rule into per-position copy and compare, Titan's proven strength, using copy-balanced fresh data, a matched direct-answer control and a 10-bit OOD test. Decimal-to-binary conversion at 0.6B is the main risk, and the token cost is about 10x per step.

scores.title: Generator–verifier gap triage: can any scorer recognise gold among the error forms the models actually produce?
scores.rationale: It is cheap (1 GPU h) and produces a useful routing table, but the evidence already points to decomposition for R and P, where gold is rarely produced. It runs on heavily used pilot data and adds no capability itself.

scores.title: Confidence-gated deferral and adapter routing: transfer BWM F-03 to RCWM per step, and use it to remove the T2 adapter's off-task drift
scores.rationale: Its own predictions put the per-step deferral gains near null, and the prompt router mostly operationalises the ledger-scoped packaging already decided. On templated prompts the router is close to trivial, so the only informative part is the near-domain and paraphrase precision/recall.

scores.title: [SPECULATIVE] Train on certified self-labels: distil the verified inference stack back into the model without oracle labels
scores.rationale: Oracle labels are free in these synthetic domains, the idea depends on two unproven pipelines, and certified labels are biased toward steps the model already gets right. The expected intelligence gain per GPU hour is low.

scores.title: 1. Skill-block rule-coverage LoRA: retrain T2 only in blocks 8-15 (complement arm 16-27), then stack it on the L8-15 core
scores.rationale: A cheap PEFT knob grounded in R12 and R14 that should keep the ledger skill with less drift and adds a mechanism dissociation. It is mainly a retention gain, though, and R14 shows that two thirds of the drift sits in 8-15, so the payoff is modest.

scores.title: 2. Targets matched to the mechanism for the rules T2 never learned: in-step scratchpads for register mix/wrap; bit-string states with an explicit applicable flag for prerequisite
scores.rationale: This is the best-designed attack on the unlearned computed-value rules. Fresh data puts 300 rows on mix, caps copy targets at 35% and oversamples carries. A plain-target arm separates format from data and an untargeted arm separates targeting, and a rule-edge OOD bank is included, all for about 4 GPU h.

scores.title: 3. Retention frontier for the T2 adapter: inference-time dose scaling vs KL-anchored retraining (plus a speculative Supa-anchored 'drift payback')
scores.rationale: The alpha sweep is cheap and informative, but the work optimises retention for an adapter that will stay unmerged and scoped. The Supa-payback arm risks erasing the skill, because drift and skill share blocks 8-15.

scores.title: 4. Rollout distillation limited by depth: a 2-event 'jump' adapter, and a test of a block-budget prediction for single-pass k-step consequences (partly speculative)
scores.rationale: The dependent-vs-commuting stratification is a neat test of latent composition depth, but the 8-blocks-per-step budget is a weak heuristic. Chaining already works cheaply, and the expected durable gain is small.

scores.title: 5. Localise the BWM adapters by block (R12 method) and build a multi-skill Titan core: routed vs summed vs block-disjoint composition of T2 + BW_Fdelta (+ port to L8-15)
scores.rationale: This is mostly a packaging question with likely JSON-format crosstalk between adapters. Routing already preserves both skills, so it adds little new reasoning ability.

scores.title: 6. A repair only possible while unmerged: per-step confidence-gated deferral between adapter ON and OFF for the prerequisite copy shortcut (BWM F-03 transplanted; speculative, cheap)
scores.rationale: Both arms implement wrong P rules (copy vs integer addition), the shortcut is confident (F-06), and the idea itself predicts under 30% recovery. At best it chooses between two non-rules.

scores.title: [Rank 1] Rule or trigger token? A sealed ledger generalisation map for the T2 adapter: unseen non-posted statuses, unseen operands and magnitudes, more or renamed accounts, and format perturbations
scores.rationale: For about 1 GPU h it tests whether the one confirmed skill is a rule or a trigger, and where it breaks: unseen statuses, 4-5-digit balances, unseen operands, more or renamed accounts. This is exactly the BWM F-01 out-of-range failure mode, and the result would redirect all later data work, though it adds no capability on its own.

scores.title: [Rank 2] Long horizons (k = 8 and 16): magnitude-clamped vs natural chains, the per-step product law, and whether the model's errors are decision-benign
scores.rationale: Long-horizon and decision-benign-error measurements are relevant to planning, but the product law is close to true by construction for memoryless chains, and the study only measures existing ability.

scores.title: [Rank 3] Seed-consensus certificates: does agreement between the three T2 adapters flag world-model errors on fresh and out-of-range inputs, and does per-step majority voting extend the horizon?
scores.rationale: This is a cheaper, better-falsifiable version of the ensemble idea, and its registered prediction that seeds share shortcuts is informative. Any gain is still 3x inference compute on ledger, not a durable capability.

scores.title: [Rank 4] Is the LM's edge out of range? Titan+T2 vs matched-label no-LLM learners (S-roll MLP and a from-scratch digit-token transformer) on the OOD and long-horizon strata
scores.rationale: With no GPU cost it answers the strategic question of whether the LM route is worth it out of range, but it makes no model smarter, depends on Ranks 1-2, and carries fairness and tuning disputes.

scores.title: [Rank 5] A re-mintable, correctness-based retention suite, and calibrating KL drift against actual capability loss
scores.rationale: Measuring lost abilities by correctness rather than KL proxies is durable infrastructure for the retention goal, at under 1 GPU h. It also stops retention claims from spending scarce confirmation banks.

scores.title: [Rank 6, speculative] Does one-step rule training compose latently? Single-shot k-step answers and teacher-forced likelihood ranking under the T2 adapter
scores.rationale: PREREG-1 already closed the latent route, and the idea itself expects a negative result, so the information and intelligence gain per GPU hour are low.

scores.title: FlagWorld bridge: give the prerequisite simulator BWM's explicit-legality bit/delta interface instead of Titan's integer mask
scores.rationale: It is likely to fix P, with a rebalanced-integer control and a 12-flag size-OOD test. But the bitstring interface does much of the work, and C-delta has a parser apply the change, so less of the gain is the model learning to reason about integer masks than with the binary scratchpad.

scores.title: Search under the learned simulator: does PREREG-2's near-oracle ledger model survive BWM-style planning, and can BWM's confidence signal curb exploitation?
scores.rationale: Checking for model exploitation under wider search is a real planning question and guards against benchmark gaming. The domain is a toy linear-goal ledger, though, and the measured gains in planning ability are likely modest for 3 GPU h.

scores.title: Core-transfer test: is Titan-Sparse (or L8-15) a better substrate than Supa for learning new world models?
scores.rationale: It helps choose the substrate, but it is single-seed, Blocksworld F may sit near ceiling on every base, and it produces no new capability.

scores.title: One shared world-model adapter across domains, localised to blocks 8-15 (unified-core test; partly speculative)
scores.rationale: A unified multi-domain core would be valuable, but at 4 GPU h it has many confounds (token imbalance, long Blocksworld outputs), and the interesting cross-domain precondition transfer is speculative.

scores.title: Infrastructure exchange: sealed-bank confirmation of BWM's deferral gate, plus a selectivity-controlled internal-signal gate for its confident below-range errors
scores.rationale: Sealed confirmation of a training-free repair, plus a shared OOD, rule-edge and size-OOD suite, is cheap and anti-gaming. The learned internal-signal gate is likely negative, and the bundle is broad.

scores.title: Micro-step rollout for composite operations: chain BWM-proven primitive ops inside one register event (speculative)
scores.rationale: This is a cheap (1.5 GPU h), focused, controlled test of whether intermediate primitives make mix and wrap learnable on fresh mix-heavy data, with a retention check. Mix fails even without wrap, so decomposition is the right lever, but it covers register only.

scores.title: 1. Put the intermediate in the answer: trace-in-JSON targets for rules that need a computed value (register conditional, mix/mod-97, prerequisite applicability)
scores.rationale: Strong design for this machine: it re-renders the identical 1,501 T2 events, includes a filler-token control that separates extra decode compute from supervised intermediates, sets the go rule in advance with three-seed agreement, and confirms on a fresh sealed bank; the drawbacks are that 5 GPU-h covers only the screen and that training the R and P traces in one arm needs pinned parsers.

scores.title: 2. Shortcut-neutralised, minimal-pair prerequisite data to break the copy shortcut
scores.rationale: Cheap and sharply falsifiable: the four heuristics are rejection-sampled to exactly 50%, the thresholds are numeric (false copy <=0.25, app-del >=0.30, pairs >=0.50), P-only evals take about 15 min, and seed agreement and a fresh sealed bank are required; multiplicity across its five predictions is not Holm-controlled, and a 'cannot learn bits' null is likely but still informative.

scores.title: 3. Separate rule learning from frame adaptation and targeting: self-distillation, natural-marginal (untargeted) and void-dose controls for PREREG-2's gain
scores.rationale: It directly closes a limit that PREREG-2 itself registered, using clean controls (SD, NAT, a dose ladder) preregistered before training on a fresh sealed ledger bank; about 13 trainings will exceed the stated 4 GPU-h, and the SD contrast is close to a foregone pass because Titan's own labels are wrong on void.

scores.title: 4. Rule or token? Lexical and rule-text counterfactual probes for 'status is not posted', then counterfactual-augmented training
scores.rationale: Part (a) is a roughly 0.6 GPU-h zero-training probe with predictions written before reading and a payoff either way, and part (b) uses held-out words and paraphrases on a sealed bank; the 0.5-0.9 band is left undecided, near-miss golds such as 'posted?' are arguable, and it is largely a subset of eval Rank 1.

scores.title: 5. Matched-budget data-efficiency curves: Titan LoRA vs the S-roll MLP vs a copy-capable symbolic learner
scores.rationale: It builds on existing S-roll code and addresses a registered PREREG-2 limit, with Holm-controlled contrasts on a fresh bank; N50 estimated from five curve points is noisy, the epoch/step and DEV-checkpoint fairness confounds are only partly handled, and the third learner is under-specified.

scores.title: 6. Rehearsal data inside the rule-coverage LoRA to stop cumulative drift (speculative on magnitude)
scores.rationale: The primaries are falsifiable (regret non-inferiority +0.03 and drift ratio <1.25), there is a dilution control, and it is careful about the reserved instruments (456, HSKILL); however, the supply of the preservation slice and of fresh off-task prompts is uncertain, and KL and agreement remain proxies for forgetting.

scores.title: Disagreement-certified verification to stretch ledger rollouts to 8-16 steps (T2 adapter, no new training)
scores.rationale: Well controlled (best-single-seed, compute-matched self-consistency and random-selection nulls; Holm on per-parent bootstrap), and my read-only check of t2_eval supports the premise (ledger unanimity 218/240 with 218/218 correct, gold among candidates on 19/22 disagreements); a 50-parent bank is thin, and the selector depends on a separate triage step.

scores.title: Zero-training register fix: mod-97 output tool, a comparison sub-query, and model-written expressions run by a calculator
scores.rationale: Cheap (CPU prompt development plus about 2 GPU-h), with tiers kept separate so tools are not counted as skill and good rule-reading guards (held-out op, mod-89); the multi-component pipeline tuned on DEV leaves many researcher degrees of freedom, and the thresholds (+0.25 k=4 exact) are optimistic for 0.6B expression writing.

scores.title: Binary scratchpad inside each step for the prerequisite family, against a direct-answer LoRA trained on the same rows
scores.rationale: A clean two-arm contrast (same rows, seed and order; only the target representation differs) with Holm-controlled primaries against the copy floor, a forgetting guard and token accounting; the 10-bit OOD test is confounded by the fixed 8-position format, and the roughly 10x decode cost lengthens chain evals under the duty cap.

scores.title: Generator–verifier gap triage: can any scorer recognise gold among the error forms the models actually produce?
scores.rationale: A cheap prefill-only run (about 1 GPU-h) with pre-stated predictions and a written routing table that decides later spend, and it is honest that it is non-confirmatory on exposed pilot data; likelihood format confounds need the planned +-1 foils, and earlier likelihood jobs were the hottest on this GPU.

scores.title: Confidence-gated deferral and adapter routing: transfer BWM F-03 to RCWM per step, and use it to remove the T2 adapter's off-task drift
scores.rationale: Part (b) validates the D-28(b) ledger-scoped packaging, but its primary KL ratio is nearly guaranteed by construction if the router works; part (a) predicts near-null gains and depends on logs from other runs, and keeping Supa and Titan resident strains the 70% VRAM cap.

scores.title: [SPECULATIVE] Train on certified self-labels: distil the verified inference stack back into the model without oracle labels
scores.rationale: It has a sensible label-precision stop rule and SL/OR/UL controls, but it is contingent on two earlier ideas succeeding, label selection bias is hard to control, the 3 GPU-h is an underestimate, and it cites about 330 mix rows when T2 had 175.

scores.title: 1. Skill-block rule-coverage LoRA: retrain T2 only in blocks 8-15 (complement arm 16-27), then stack it on the L8-15 core
scores.rationale: Only layers_to_transform changes, so it reuses the frozen T2 recipe and eval stages; it adds capacity (r48) and A827 controls, a three-seed gate, two Holm primaries (non-inferiority +0.05 and drift ratio <0.80) on a fresh bank and a fresh off-task draw, and is very feasible; the PORT and STACK arms must wait for L1.

scores.title: 2. Targets matched to the mechanism for the rules T2 never learned: in-step scratchpads for register mix/wrap; bit-string states with an explicit applicable flag for prerequisite
scores.rationale: It includes the untargeted U-natural control and a plain-format arm, with a seed gate and Holm primaries on sealed banks; the primary contrasts are against OFF rather than T3-plain, so format attribution is only secondary, and R and P changes in one arm plus parser changes add moving parts.

scores.title: 3. Retention frontier for the T2 adapter: inference-time dose scaling vs KL-anchored retraining (plus a speculative Supa-anchored 'drift payback')
scores.rationale: Phase A is a clean, training-free alpha sweep, and the matched-drift superiority test is well posed, with disable_adapter() teachers that avoid VRAM growth; anchor-prompt supply after exclusions is an open operator question, the KL-loss training needs new code, and three phases stretch the turn budget.

scores.title: 4. Rollout distillation limited by depth: a 2-event 'jump' adapter, and a test of a block-budget prediction for single-pass k-step consequences (partly speculative)
scores.rationale: Falsifiable, with a dependency-stratified interaction contrast and a splice probe, but the depth-budget heuristic is weakly identified (a plateau can come from data or optimisation), and the +0.03 non-inferiority margin against a 0.056-regret comparator is very tight.

scores.title: 5. Localise the BWM adapters by block (R12 method) and build a multi-skill Titan core: routed vs summed vs block-disjoint composition of T2 + BW_Fdelta (+ port to L8-15)
scores.rationale: Feasible on CPU and GPU with McNemar-based non-inferiority, but a -0.02 margin on BW_F exact with 60 keys per size is underpowered (one error is 1.7 pp), the CPU grading of long Blocksworld outputs is probably understated, and it requires cross-session use of BWM's frozen artifacts.

scores.title: 6. A repair only possible while unmerged: per-step confidence-gated deferral between adapter ON and OFF for the prerequisite copy shortcut (BWM F-03 transplanted; speculative, cheap)
scores.rationale: Cheap, with a clear go/no-go and a pre-stated F-06 expectation, random-deferral and oracle-gate controls; but gate selection uses exposed t2_eval and 28 pilot parents, P regret headroom is low, and the expected outcome is a null.

scores.title: [Rank 1] Rule or trigger token? A sealed ledger generalisation map for the T2 adapter: unseen non-posted statuses, unseen operands and magnitudes, more or renamed accounts, and format perturbations
scores.rationale: The best fit to this lens: zero training, about 1-1.5 GPU-h, posted twins, OFF, Supa and copy-floor controls, a pinned scorer validated on golds, a three-way decision rule with Wilson bounds in all seeds, Holm McNemar primaries, a hashed analysis and explicit exclusions (L1 OOD bank, HSKILL skipped by name).

scores.title: [Rank 2] Long horizons (k = 8 and 16): magnitude-clamped vs natural chains, the per-step product law, and whether the model's errors are decision-benign
scores.rationale: A precise TOST equivalence prediction from a disjoint calibration set, a floor-binding check, resumable stages and a noisy-oracle comparator make it well posed at about 2 GPU-h; rejection-sampling the clamped stratum shifts the event mix, and the run may span two turns.

scores.title: [Rank 3] Seed-consensus certificates: does agreement between the three T2 adapters flag world-model errors on fresh and out-of-range inputs, and does per-step majority voting extend the horizon?
scores.rationale: Cheap, reuses the Rank 1-2 banks, and its failure-mode prediction (c) is falsifiable and already plausible (on t2_eval, unanimity precision is 1.00 for ledger but only 0.73 for P and 0.76 for register); 'all three seed-pair orders' is ill-defined for three-way unanimity, and it largely duplicates the disagreement-certified idea.

scores.title: [Rank 4] Is the LM's edge out of range? Titan+T2 vs matched-label no-LLM learners (S-roll MLP and a from-scratch digit-token transformer) on the OOD and long-horizon strata
scores.rationale: It costs no GPU, registers a symmetric claim rule and hashes checkpoints before Titan's OOD outputs are read; a from-scratch transformer on about 629 rows is a weak and dispute-prone comparator, strata the learners cannot represent make the comparison asymmetric, and CPU contention with the peer and the 12 GB RAM floor remain constraints.

scores.title: [Rank 5] A re-mintable, correctness-based retention suite, and calibrating KL drift against actual capability loss
scores.rationale: Code-graded generator banks that are minted after the freeze would end the scarcity of instruments, and the McNemar per-category design and KL-AUROC prediction are falsifiable; building eight validated generators is substantial engineering, and 75 items per category gives modest power at a 5-of-75 margin.

scores.title: [Rank 6, speculative] Does one-step rule training compose latently? Single-shot k-step answers and teacher-forced likelihood ranking under the T2 adapter
scores.rationale: Cheap, shares the Rank 2 bank and reuses the frozen D-09 instrument, with two registered directional predictions; the multi-step frame was never trained for T2 and token-length effects confound it, and the expected negative gives limited information.

scores.title: FlagWorld bridge: give the prerequisite simulator BWM's explicit-legality bit/delta interface instead of Titan's integer mask
scores.rationale: The A-int arm cleanly separates data rebalancing from interface format, with Holm primaries on a fresh bank, a structural/bit-permutation dedupe, a parity gate and size-OOD as the cleanest test; three formats plus seeds exceed 3.5 GPU-h, and the delta parser must be disclosed as part of the method.

scores.title: Search under the learned simulator: does PREREG-2's near-oracle ledger model survive BWM-style planning, and can BWM's confidence signal curb exploitation?
scores.rationale: Absolute loss as primary, lambda fixed on DEV, prefix caching and a parity gate are rigorous choices; P1 holds almost by construction (winner's curse), about 47k step generations make 3 GPU-h tight, and the per-goal beam-search cost may force post-hoc restriction.

scores.title: Core-transfer test: is Titan-Sparse (or L8-15) a better substrate than Supa for learning new world models?
scores.rationale: A clear grid with a fixed recipe and paired McNemar, but a non-inferiority margin of -0.03 with about 60 keys per size is underpowered, it is single-seed at first, it touches L8-15 and BWM data while L1 and B2 are running, and CPU grading of long outputs is slow.

scores.title: One shared world-model adapter across domains, localised to blocks 8-15 (unified-core test; partly speculative)
scores.rationale: Broad and multi-programme: joint data reweighting, evaluations across four domains with tight -0.03 margins, a new 450-prompt off-task draw and a speculative transfer claim; 4 GPU-h is an underestimate, and the preregistration is deferred to whatever replicates, so its falsifiability is weak.

scores.title: Infrastructure exchange: sealed-bank confirmation of BWM's deferral gate, plus a selectivity-controlled internal-signal gate for its confident below-range errors
scores.rationale: Part (a) is excellent (frozen band, never-used limits, Holm m=2, about 1 GPU-h) and part (b) has shuffled-label and rule-ceiling controls, but the WMCS-1 suite and the RCWM dedupe are open-ended infrastructure that dilutes a sharp confirmatory test.

scores.title: Micro-step rollout for composite operations: chain BWM-proven primitive ops inside one register event (speculative)
scores.rationale: Cheap (1.5 GPU-h), with a stated go threshold, seed replication, Holm primaries on a sealed R bank and a retention check; it has no filler-token control to separate extra decode compute from supervised intermediates, and it overlaps heavily with the trace and scratchpad ideas.

scores.title: 1. Put the intermediate in the answer: trace-in-JSON targets for rules that need a computed value (register conditional, mix/mod-97, prerequisite applicability)
scores.rationale: This trains new unmerged adapters that move Titan off its trained bare-JSON frame. That invites trace-format bleed and extra drift, which only off-task KL catches; it is the largest training spend (5 h), with 2-3x decode tokens of thermal exposure; and the screen re-reads already-seen t2_eval/supp.

scores.title: 2. Shortcut-neutralised, minimal-pair prerequisite data to break the copy shortcut
scores.rationale: It keeps the trained output format and registers a ledger no-harm guard (regret loss at most 0.03) plus off-task KL, but per-family upweighting may raise drift and the plan needs about 4.5 GPU h of new adapters.

scores.title: 3. Separate rule learning from frame adaptation and targeting: self-distillation, natural-marginal (untargeted) and void-dose controls for PREREG-2's gain
scores.rationale: These are diagnostic adapters only, never packaged, and off-task KL is measured. The arm count (SD and NAT at 3 seeds each, plus 5 or more dose arms) makes 4 GPU h look optimistic, so thermal and lease exposure is higher than stated.

scores.title: 4. Rule or token? Lexical and rule-text counterfactual probes for 'status is not posted', then counterfactual-augmented training
scores.rationale: Part (a) is a cheap zero-training probe with low risk. Part (b) trains on altered and inverted system prompts that fight Titan's prior and change the frame, a plausible drift and instruction-following side effect with no explicit off-task guard.

scores.title: 5. Matched-budget data-efficiency curves: Titan LoRA vs the S-roll MLP vs a copy-capable symbolic learner
scores.rationale: These are research-only L-only adapters with no packaging path and no drift guard. The real cost is many short training jobs (5 N x 2 seeds, plus fixed-step and 3 confirm seeds) and extra CPU lanes against the shared RAM floor.

scores.title: 6. Rehearsal data inside the rule-coverage LoRA to stop cumulative drift (speculative on magnitude)
scores.rationale: It targets retention directly with a registered cumulative-drift bound and a fresh off-task draw that explicitly excludes the 248, the 456, the HSKILL pools and the rehearsal pool. The residual risk is that slice replay overlaps a retention instrument or that Supa targets undo Titan's delta near JSON.

scores.title: Disagreement-certified verification to stretch ledger rollouts to 8-16 steps (T2 adapter, no new training)
scores.rationale: There is no training and the adapters stay unmerged and multi-loaded in one process, so retention risk is nil. A 5 GPU h run at up to 3x calls per step, with long 12-step chains, is a sizeable thermal and TDR exposure on the shared laptop.

scores.title: Zero-training register fix: mod-97 output tool, a comparison sub-query, and model-written expressions run by a calculator
scores.rationale: There are no weight changes and the GPU budget is modest. Risks are operational: a CPU prompt-tuning lane that loads Supa and Titan-OFF against the RAM floor, and the need to keep the expression calculator strictly sandboxed (named-free integer grammar, as specified).

scores.title: Binary scratchpad inside each step for the prerequisite family, against a direct-answer LoRA trained on the same rows
scores.rationale: It trains two new unmerged adapters and keeps the PREREG-2 forgetting guard, but a roughly 10x token scratchpad lengthens chains and thermal exposure, and the new long-format target may bleed off-task.

scores.title: Generator–verifier gap triage: can any scorer recognise gold among the error forms the models actually produce?
scores.rationale: This is inference only, with no retention risk, and it confines selection to DEV. The earlier likelihood job coincided with an 89-91 C excursion and a TDR, so 45k prefills need the small-batch, watchdog-gated regime the idea itself specifies.

scores.title: Confidence-gated deferral and adapter routing: transfer BWM F-03 to RCWM per step, and use it to remove the T2 adapter's off-task drift
scores.rationale: The router is a strong retention safeguard that preserves the unmerged design and is tested on fresh near-domain negatives. Training it on R14's 248 permanently burns that drift instrument (which includes 20 HSKILL-002-pool prompts), and co-resident Supa plus Titan risks VRAM paging under the 70% cap.

scores.title: [SPECULATIVE] Train on certified self-labels: distil the verified inference stack back into the model without oracle labels
scores.rationale: Self-training on model outputs risks error amplification and loss of diversity (expert iteration). It adds further adapters and drift, and it depends on two unbuilt pipelines; the 0.98 precision stop rule and the PREREG-2 guard are its only safeguards.

scores.title: 1. Skill-block rule-coverage LoRA: retrain T2 only in blocks 8-15 (complement arm 16-27), then stack it on the L8-15 core
scores.rationale: It aims to cut adapter drift, with a registered KL-ratio primary on a fresh off-task draw that excludes the 248, the 456 and the HSKILL pools. It waits for L1 before touching the L8-15 weights, though phase 1 re-reads the partly spent 248 and STACK builds on an unpromoted core.

scores.title: 2. Targets matched to the mechanism for the rules T2 never learned: in-step scratchpads for register mix/wrap; bit-string states with an explicit applicable flag for prerequisite
scores.rationale: It registers a ledger non-inferiority guard and a fresh-draw forgetting guard. New output formats, parser changes and longer decodes add drift and thermal exposure, and the change of output format could disturb existing JSON behaviour.

scores.title: 3. Retention frontier for the T2 adapter: inference-time dose scaling vs KL-anchored retraining (plus a speculative Supa-anchored 'drift payback')
scores.rationale: It is designed to shrink drift. Phase A is training-free PEFT scaling with no merge, and the in-process disable_adapter teacher avoids a second model in VRAM. Residual risks are anchor prompts from the preservation slice possibly touching retention instruments, and phase A reusing the 248.

scores.title: 4. Rollout distillation limited by depth: a 2-event 'jump' adapter, and a test of a block-budget prediction for single-pass k-step consequences (partly speculative)
scores.rationale: Multi-event training may degrade one-step skill and adds new adapters, and unlike most training ideas it registers no off-task drift or forgetting guard.

scores.title: 5. Localise the BWM adapters by block (R12 method) and build a multi-skill Titan core: routed vs summed vs block-disjoint composition of T2 + BW_Fdelta (+ port to L8-15)
scores.rationale: Summed adapters invite cross-skill interference, format crosstalk and additive drift, and the work points toward an always-on multi-skill core that D-28(b) deliberately avoids. It is mitigated by staying unmerged, a CPU-first phase A that still loads the RAM budget, and per-adapter KL.

scores.title: 6. A repair only possible while unmerged: per-step confidence-gated deferral between adapter ON and OFF for the prerequisite copy shortcut (BWM F-03 transplanted; speculative, cheap)
scores.rationale: It needs no training and 1 GPU h, uses pilot data only for selection, and explicitly exploits and reinforces the unmerged, recoverable-base packaging policy.

scores.title: [Rank 1] Rule or trigger token? A sealed ledger generalisation map for the T2 adapter: unseen non-posted statuses, unseen operands and magnitudes, more or renamed accounts, and format perturbations
scores.rationale: It is eval only at about 1 GPU h, with no weight changes. The bank build skips HSKILL_CONFIRM_V2 by name and excludes the spent L1 OOD bank, and it surfaces out-of-range shortcuts before any packaging decision.

scores.title: [Rank 2] Long horizons (k = 8 and 16): magnitude-clamped vs natural chains, the per-step product law, and whether the model's errors are decision-benign
scores.rationale: There is no training and the instruments are fresh and sealed. About 1.7 h of long chains with 160-token caps, possible magnitude blow-ups and a run spanning two turns add moderate thermal and resume risk, which resumable stages mitigate.

scores.title: [Rank 3] Seed-consensus certificates: does agreement between the three T2 adapters flag world-model errors on fresh and out-of-range inputs, and does per-step majority voting extend the horizon?
scores.rationale: It is inference only on banks shared with Ranks 1-2 and makes no weight changes. Voting triples the calls per step, but the stated budget is about 1 GPU h.

scores.title: [Rank 4] Is the LM's edge out of range? Titan+T2 vs matched-label no-LLM learners (S-roll MLP and a from-scratch digit-token transformer) on the OOD and long-horizon strata
scores.rationale: It needs zero GPU and makes no Titan weight changes, and learners are hashed before Titan outputs are read. CPU lanes compete with the peer for RAM, which has caused emergencies before (I-14); the D-39 floor must hold.

scores.title: [Rank 5] A re-mintable, correctness-based retention suite, and calibrating KL drift against actual capability loss
scores.rationale: It directly builds the missing safeguard: a correctness-graded, re-mintable retention instrument that stops spending the last unspent banks and tests whether the KL gates are miscalibrated. It is cheap and inference-only, with registry entries at first use.

scores.title: [Rank 6, speculative] Does one-step rule training compose latently? Single-shot k-step answers and teacher-forced likelihood ranking under the T2 adapter
scores.rationale: It is eval only at about 1 GPU h on a shared fresh bank, with no retention risk. The only operational note is that likelihood jobs have previously run hot, so the watchdog regime applies.

scores.title: FlagWorld bridge: give the prerequisite simulator BWM's explicit-legality bit/delta interface instead of Titan's integer mask
scores.rationale: It trains three new adapters with a new output format and longer decodes but registers no off-task drift or forgetting guard. The contamination controls are good: HSKILL is skipped by name, there is a parity gate, and bit-permutation dedupe is applied.

scores.title: Search under the learned simulator: does PREREG-2's near-oracle ledger model survive BWM-style planning, and can BWM's confidence signal curb exploitation?
scores.rationale: There is no training, the banks are fresh and sealed, and a byte-parity gate guards the changed generation code. A 3 GPU h tree-search run with prefix caching is moderate thermal exposure within one lease turn.

scores.title: Core-transfer test: is Titan-Sparse (or L8-15) a better substrate than Supa for learning new world models?
scores.rationale: It trains research adapters across three bases, including the unpromoted L8-15, and names its interference risks with frozen L1 and BWM B2 assets. The new fresh off-task draw is a good safeguard, but the multi-base GPU grid plus CPU grading lanes is a broad operational footprint.

scores.title: One shared world-model adapter across domains, localised to blocks 8-15 (unified-core test; partly speculative)
scores.rationale: Joint cross-domain training risks interference between per-domain skills, and its framing toward an always-on or merged core cuts against D-28's recoverable-base policy. Long Blocksworld supervision has paged VRAM before (BWM I-02); the J-loc arm and the fresh 450-prompt drift draw partly offset this.

scores.title: Infrastructure exchange: sealed-bank confirmation of BWM's deferral gate, plus a selectivity-controlled internal-signal gate for its confident below-range errors
scores.rationale: It strengthens anti-contamination infrastructure (renaming dedupe on old banks, a sealed joint suite that never reuses L1 or HSKILL instruments) and confirms a training-free repair. Its GPU use is small, though WMCS-1's breadth raises bookkeeping risk around reserved instruments.

scores.title: Micro-step rollout for composite operations: chain BWM-proven primitive ops inside one register event (speculative)
scores.rationale: It trains new adapters with a roughly 3x-token scratchpad format. Retention is checked only on in-family swap and add, with no off-task drift or forgetting guard.
